title: Semi-supervised machine learning identifies two strong gravitational lenses in the Deep Lens Survey
summary: A ResNetV2-based semi-supervised workflow ranked images from the 20-square-degree Deep Lens Survey and surfaced two Grade-A lens systems for follow-up. Keck spectroscopy secured a source redshift of z=1.81 for DLS212072337, while DLS432021848 has only a tentative single-line redshift but supporting high-resolution Hubble morphology; the paper counts both as lensing systems, with the latter less secure. The broader visually inspected list contains additional candidates, not confirmed lenses.
ai_technology: ResNetV2 neural network with semi-supervised MixMatch or Pi-Model and GAN-based image augmentation
organization: University of California, Davis; University of California, Santa Cruz; University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: A ResNetV2-based semi-supervised workflow ranked images from the 20-square-degree Deep Lens Survey and surfaced two Grade-A lens systems for follow-up.
evidence.unknown: This is a paper-level result about a survey search and validated lens identification, not a claim that all 22 visually graded systems are confirmed. DLS212072337 has secure spectroscopic source and deflector redshifts; DLS432021848 has an ambiguous single emission line and is judged likely from HST morphology rather than conclusive spectroscopy. arXiv version 1 is a preprint; current full text was updated in 2026.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked galaxy-survey images for strong-lensing morphology; the top-ranked systems were then human-inspected and followed up spectroscopically/imaged to validate lensing.
